([[Rochester Hills, Michigan]]) | college = *[[Duquesne Dukes men's basketball|Duquesne]] (2016–2017) *[[Toledo Rockets men's basketball|Toledo]] (2018–2021) | draft_year = 2021 | career_start = 2021 | years1 = 2021–2022 | team1 = [[Limburg United]] | years2 = 2022–2023 | team2 = [[Imortal Basket|Imortal Luzigas]] | years3 = 2023–2025 | team3 = [[CD Estela|Grupo Alega Cantabria]] | years4 = 2025–present | team4 = [[CB Menorca|Bàsquet Menorca]] | highlights = * [[Belgian Basketball Cup|Belgian Cup]] winner (2022) *Second-team All-[[Mid-American Conference|MAC]] (2021) *MAC All-Defensive Team (2021) }} '''Spencer Phillip Littleson''' (born May 29, 1998) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for [[CB Menorca|Bàsquet Menorca]] of the [[Primera FEB]]. He played [[college basketball]] for [[Toledo Rockets men's basketball|Toledo]] and [[Duquesne Dukes men's basketball|Duquesne]]. ==High school career== Littleson attended [[Rochester Adams High School]]. He grew from 5'10 to 6'3 during his freshman season.{{cite news |last1=Purcell |first1=Jared |title=Mr. Basketball finalist: Rochester Adams' Spencer Littleson strives to be 'the hardest worker' |url=https://www.mlive.com/highschoolsports/article/mr-basketball-finalist-rochester-adams-spencer-littleson-strives-to-be-the-hardest-worker/ |access-date=July 2, 2021 |work=[[MLive]] |date=March 16, 2016}} As a senior, he averaged 25.1 points, 6.3 rebounds, 3.2 assists, and 2.0 steals per game. Littleson finished third in the voting for 2016 [[Mr. Basketball of Michigan]]. He committed to play college basketball at [[Duquesne Dukes men's basketball|Duquesne]].{{cite news |last1=Buckey |first1=Brian |title=Littleson joins men's hoops program at UT |url=https://www.toledoblade.com/sports/college/2017/05/16/Former-Duquense-guard-Spencer-Littleson-joins-men-s-hoops-program-at-University-of-Toledo/stories/20170515261 |access-date=July 2, 2021 |work=[[The Blade (Toledo, Ohio)|The Blade]] |date=May 16, 2017}} ==College career== As a freshman at Duquesne, Littleson averaged 1.6 points and 1.1 rebounds. Following the season he transferred to [[Toledo Rockets men's basketball|Toledo]]. Toledo coach [[Tod Kowalczyk]] called him an "unbelievable worker" and said they should have recruited him out of high school.{{cite news |last1=Rowland |first1=Kyle |title=UT senior leaders Jackson, Littleson have one more go-round at Savage Arena |url=https://www.toledoblade.com/sports/ut/2021/03/04/mens-basketball-marreon-jackson-spencer-littleson-toledo-senior-leaders-last-game-savage-arena/stories/20210304100 |access-date=July 2, 2021 |work=[[The Blade (Toledo, Ohio)|The Blade]] |date=March 5, 2021}} As a sophomore, Littleson averaged 4.2 points and 2.2 rebounds per game.{{cite news |last1=Buckey |first1=Brian |title=Toledo's Spencer Littleson producing in expanded role |url=https://www.toledoblade.com/sports/ut/2019/12/11/Toledo-basketball-s-Littleson-producing-in-expanded-role/stories/20191211133 |access-date=July 2, 2021 |work=[[The Blade (Toledo, Ohio)|The Blade]] |date=December 11, 2019}} On November 10, 2019, he scored a career-high 27 points in an 96-70 win against [[Marshall Thundering Herd men's basketball|Marshall]].{{cite news |title=Littleson scores 27 to carry Toledo past Marshall 96-70 |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401172564 |access-date=July 2, 2021 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=November 10, 2019}} Littleson averaged 10.5 points per game as a junior.{{cite web |title=UT Rockets Finalize 2020-21 Men's Basketball Schedule |url=https://www.toledo.com/news/2020/10/27/daily-dose/ut-rockets-finalize-2020-21-men-s-basketball-schedule/ |website=Toledo.com |access-date=July 2, 2021 |date=October 27, 2020}} As a senior, Littleson averaged 13.4 points and 3.2 rebounds per game. He was named to the Second Team All-[[Mid-American Conference|MAC]] and the MAC All-Defensive Team.{{cite news |title=Former Toledo guard Littleson signs with Belgian professional team |url=https://www.toledoblade.com/sports/ut/2021/06/29/former-toledo-guard-spencer-littleson-signs-with-belgian-professional-team/stories/20210629198 |access-date=July 2, 2021 |work=[[The Blade (Toledo, Ohio)|The Blade]] |date=June 29, 2021}} Littleson led Division I with a school-record 103 three-point field goals and finished second nationally with a 47.2 three-point percentage. He was selected to participate in the State Farm 3-Point Championship.{{cite web |title=Toledo Men's Basketball's Spencer Littleson to Compete in State Farm 3-Point Championships |url=https://getsomemaction.com/news/2021/3/24/toledo-mens-basketballs-spencer-littleson-to-compete-in-state-farm-3-point-championships.aspx |website=[[Mid-American Conference]] |access-date=July 2, 2021 |date=March 24, 2021}} ==Professional career== On June 28, 2021, Littleson signed his first professional contract with [[Limburg United]] of the [[BNXT League]].{{cite web |last=Buyse|first=Peter|title=Limburg signs rookie Spencer Littleson in his first year in pro basketball|url=https://www.eurobasket.com/Belgium/news/691206/Limburg-signs-rookie-Spencer-Littleson-in-his-first-year-in-pro-basketball |website=Eurobasket |access-date=July 2, 2021 |date=June 28, 2021}} On August 28, 2022, Littleson signed with the [[Imortal Basket|Imortal Luzigas]] of the [[Liga Portuguesa de Basquetebol]].{{cite web |last=Xufre |first=Ricardo |title=Imortal lands Spencer Littleson, ex Limburg |url=https://www.eurobasket.com/Portugal/news/765562/Imortal-lands-Spencer-Littleson,-ex-Limburg |website=Eurobasket |access-date=February 6, 2023 |date=August 28, 2022}} On August 2, 2023, Littleson signed with [[CD Estela|Grupo Alega Cantabria]] of the [[LEB Oro]].{{cite web |title=Comunicado Oficial: Spencer Littleson – Grupo Alega Cantabria |url=https://grupoalegacantabria.es/2023/08/02/comunicado-oficial-spencer-littleson/ |access-date=2 August 2023 |language=es |date=2 August 2023}} On June 27, 2025, Littleson signed with [[CB Menorca|Bàsquet Menorca]] of the [[Primera FEB]].{{cite web |title=Spencer Littleson se incorpora al Hestia Menorca
